why_a_rule_at_all: Correction 3 of the design measured it: fed to the pinned binary at Lean's
DEFAULTS, 680 of a 1,000-statement sample of the mute set 'elaborated
cleanly'; with autoImplicit false and relaxedAutoImplicit false, 1 of 1,000.
The 679-statement difference is Lean auto-binding every unknown identifier
-- including the type glyph itself, which becomes an auto-bound TYPE
variable, turning a statement about the reals into a statement about an
arbitrary type. An oracle run at the defaults would certify round trips
between two elaborations of a proposition nobody wrote. So autoImplicit must
be off; with it off the surface must carry an explicit binder preamble; and
choosing binder types is semantic work. That work is this file, frozen,
rather than a decision the inverter takes at run time.
type_substitution_notes: Correction 2(b): the pinned toolchain carries no Mathlib, so `#check ℝ` and
`#check Real.sqrt` both return Unknown identifier. The review's correction,
adopted: substitute the TYPE, so the real-analysis mass is carried under a
declared domain rather than blocked. What stays blocked is Mathlib's HEAD
vocabulary, which has no core-Lean referent at all.
This is an INTERPRETATION, not a discovery. Where a statement's source
meaning is over the reals and rule R elaborates it over the rationals, that
is recorded per statement in the receipt's `interpretation_shift` field and
named in every sentence that quotes B1.
Substitution is literal, single-character, left-to-right, over the whole
source text, in the key order listed above. The four keys are pairwise
distinct single characters and no replacement value contains a key, so the
result does not depend on the order and the operation is idempotent.

harness_settings_notes: maxHeartbeats is emitted as a `set_option` line and IS part of the
acceptance definition: a statement that exhausts it is rejected, and the
budget is frozen here so it cannot be raised after a rate is read.
maxErrors is passed to the binary as `-DmaxErrors=1000000` and affects only
how many diagnostics the frontend prints. It is recorded because leaving it
at the default is a MEASUREMENT BUG, not a style choice: the pinned
toolchain stops reporting after 100 errors with `maximum number of errors
(100; from option maxErrors) reached, exiting`, and a batch prober that
infers acceptance from the ABSENCE of an error then reads every statement
after the hundredth error as accepted. Measured on this tree, that bug
alone reported 2,982 eligible where the truth is 2,319. The harness detects
the cutoff line and refuses the batch rather than trusting it.
`set_option maxErrors` inside the file does not work -- the frontend reads
the option before elaborating the file -- so the command-line form is the
only one that takes effect. Verified against the pinned binary 2026-08-24.

identifier_grammar.start_class: A-Za-z_ and the Greek letters α-ω, Α-Ω
identifier_grammar.continue_class: the start class plus 0-9, the apostrophe, and the subscripts ₀-₉ and ₐ-ₜ
note: A deliberately narrow reading of Lean's identifier grammar, chosen to
cover exactly what the committed residue carries (measured: 295 distinct
identifiers across the 4,191 residue statements, 86 across the eligible
set) rather than to be a general Lean lexer. Widening it moves the
eligibility denominator and is therefore a dated amendment with its own

binder_scan.group: a whitespace-separated run of identifiers immediately after the opener
note: The scan is LEXICAL, NOT SCOPED. Every name that appears in any binder
group anywhere in the statement is treated as bound everywhere in it.
This is a simplification and its consequence is stated rather than
hidden: an identifier that is genuinely free in one sub-term while a
same-spelled binder exists in another sub-term is NOT bound by the
preamble, and the statement is then rejected by the oracle as an unknown
identifier rather than silently reinterpreted. Rejection is the safe
direction: it costs coverage, it cannot invent a proposition.

frozen_constants.rule: an identifier containing the qualified separator `.` is NEVER bound
rule_why: A qualified name cannot be a binder name in Lean, so binding one is not a
possible reading. This rule -- not a list -- is what keeps `Real.sqrt`,
`Real.cos`, `Real.sin`, `Real.log` and every other Mathlib head out of the
preamble, so their rejection is reported as `Unknown identifier
'Real.sqrt'` and is attributable to the register's
`mathlib_head_vocabulary` entry rather than to a preamble accident.
names_why: Two groups, and they are here for different reasons.
The nine type-and-sort names are the values this rule's own substitution
produces plus core Lean's sort vocabulary; binding `Rat` at `Rat` would
shadow the type the preamble ascribes.
The sixteen bare analytic heads are Mathlib's head vocabulary spelled
without a namespace. They are named so that a statement carrying `sin x`
is rejected with `Unknown identifier 'sin'` -- attributable to
the preamble has bound `sin` to a rational. Both readings reject; only one
of them names the real reason, and the register is this cycle's product.

steps: 2. Collect BOUND names by `binder_scan` over the substituted text.
3. Collect FREE names: every identifier occurrence in the substituted text that is not bound, does not contain `.`, and is not in `frozen_constants.names`.
4. Sort the free names ascending by Unicode code point and remove duplicates.
5. If the sorted free list is empty, R(s) is the substituted text. Otherwise R(s) is `∀ ` + the free names joined by single spaces + ` : Rat, ` + the substituted text.
preamble_type_why: One type for every regenerated binder, because the preamble rule may not
do semantic work per identifier without becoming the thing it is supposed
to make honest. `Rat` rather than `Int` or `Nat` because the residue's
mass is inequalities over a field: measured on the eligible set, 2,332
type ascriptions read `Rat` against 176 `Int` and 53 `Nat`, and those two
hundred-odd come from the statement's OWN binder groups, which rule R
leaves exactly as the corpus wrote them.
A statement whose free identifiers are not rationals is therefore
rejected, not coerced. That is a coverage cost paid on purpose.
determinism: R is a pure function of the source text and this file. Same statement,
same rule file -> byte-identical R(s). The sort in step 4 is what makes
the preamble independent of the order the identifiers happen to appear in,
which is what lets R be applied independently on the original and on the
inverse output and still produce the same preamble when the rendering was
faithful. C-V4's binder-swap mutation is the measurement of how much that

why_not_branch_i: The design prefers branch (i) for one stated reason: it is 'the only route
this design has to a covered set that is not almost entirely one corpus'.
That reason was MEASURED before the branch was chosen, and it does not
survive the measurement.
A deliberately generous second interpretation was built and scored by
outcome exactly as rule R is: it rewrites the corpora's ASCII connective
vocabulary into core Lean's (`implies`/`entails` to `→`, `and` to `∧`,
`or` to `∨`, `not` to `¬`, `iff` to `↔`, `if X then Y` to `X → Y`,
`forall x.` to `∀ x,`, `exists x.` to `∃ x,`, `true`/`false` to
`True`/`False`) and binds every remaining free identifier at `Prop`. Run
against the pinned binary over the 75 statements of logic (20),
temporal_logic (15), set_theory (9), programming (9), narrative (9),
graph_theory (7) and provability (6): 13 accepted -- 12 logic rows and one
narrative row.
Thirteen statements move the covered set's composition from 99.87%
lean_workbook to 99.31% lean_workbook. Branch (i) does not deliver the
outcome that is the honest reason to prefer it, so preferring it would be
paying a second trusted artifact's review cost for a number that still
reads as 'one corpus'.
The 62 that stay out are not out for want of table rows. They are out
because they are not Lean in any alphabet: temporal_logic needs
`always`/`eventually`/`until`/`next`/`since`/`once`/`historically`,
provability needs `provable`/`falsum`/`Con` and a turnstile, set_theory
needs `inter`/`union`/`complement`/`emptyset`/`subset`/`CARD`, narrative
and programming carry English prose and Python-shaped conditional
expressions, and the eight remaining logic rows need a genuine dependent
binder (`F : α → Prop` in `(forall x. F(x)) implies F(t)`), which the
register already names as a blocked construct class. Reaching them means
AXIOMATIZING those constants inside the preamble -- and then the oracle is
adjudicating a theory this cycle wrote, which is exactly the independence
B7 exists to protect.
This is a deviation from the design's stated PREFERENCE, not from its
rule: the design requires that the branch be chosen at B0 time, before any
render, and that whichever branch is taken be recorded. Both are done
here, with the measurement that decided it.
revisit_trigger: A cycle that decides the Mathlib budget question, or a design that says
what licenses axiomatizing a modal/set-theoretic signature inside the
preamble without the oracle grading this repository's own theory. Either
reopens branch (i) with a real denominator; neither is true today.

not_claimed: Rule R is not a translation and not a discovery. It is a declared reading,
A passing identity under rule R certifies that the English determines the
term under this reading, up to what elaboration erases and what this file's
preamble regenerates. It certifies nothing about the statement's truth,
nothing about whether this reading is the one the corpus author meant, and
nothing about the English being good English.
